Interface Multiset<E>

Type Parameters:
E - the element type
All Superinterfaces:
Collection<E>, Iterable<E>
All Known Subinterfaces:
SortedMultiset<E>
All Known Implementing Classes:
HashMultiset, TreeMultiset
public interface Multiset<E> extends Collection<E>
A collection that counts how many times it contains each element: its occurrences. Equal elements are not kept apart; a multiset only knows each distinct element and its count. 
Multiset<String> words = HashMultiset.create();
words.add("foo");
words.add("bar", 2);
words.count("bar"); // 2
words.size();       // 3

The methods of Collection work on occurrences:

  • Collection.size() is the number of occurrences, up to Integer.MAX_VALUE.
  • The iterator returns each element as many times as it occurs, all occurrences of an element in a row.
  • Collection.add(Object) adds one occurrence, and always returns true.
  • Collection.remove(Object) removes one occurrence.
  • Collection.removeAll(Collection) and Collection.retainAll(Collection) remove or keep every occurrence of each element.

A count is at most Integer.MAX_VALUE; an operation that would go beyond throws IllegalArgumentException. No multiset of this library contains null.

The multisets of this library can hold more than Integer.MAX_VALUE occurrences in all: their spliterators, and so their streams, report the exact number. Their toString() writes each element once, followed by × and its count if it occurs more than once, as in [foo × 3, bar].

Since:
0.1.1

    • elementSet

      Set<E> elementSet()
      Returns a view of the distinct elements of this multiset. Removing an element from the view removes all its occurrences from this multiset. The view does not support adding elements.
      Returns:
      the distinct elements of this multiset

    • entrySet

      Set<Multiset.Entry<E>> entrySet()
      Returns a view of the distinct elements of this multiset with their counts, one entry per element, in the order of elementSet(). Removing an entry from the view removes all occurrences of its element from this multiset. The view does not support adding entries.
      Returns:
      the entries of this multiset

    • forEachEntry

      default void forEachEntry(ObjIntConsumer<? super E> action)
      Calls an action with each distinct element of this multiset and its count, in the order of elementSet().
      Parameters:
      action - the action to call

    • equals

      boolean equals(@Nullable Object o)
      Compares this multiset with an object. They are equal if the object is also a Multiset and both contain the same elements with the same counts, whatever their order or implementation.
